scanMode: regression (c91bc1a..3a96fb7, story-003) - protocol-wide value-flow reasoning over the profile + code-scan outputs; source read only to verify the two arithmetic claims below
inputsConsumed: lib/antimatter/lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol :138-155, :190-256 (read to settle the cap-arithmetic and rate-lever questions)

in: stableAmount = amount rescaled to stable decimals (pulled from msg.sender, :246)
annihilateOneCall.custody: stableAmount is pulled to Antimatter, approved to the minter (:247) and consumed by minter.mint (:251), which deposits it into config.yieldStrategy under the MINTER's ownership (PhusdStableMinter.sol:227-229). Antimatter :254 only proves the stable LEFT Antimatter. It is NOT returned, and there is no redeem/burn/withdraw path anywhere in PhusdStableMinter (grep: zero hits) - the deposit is one-way.
out: amount phUSD minted to recipient (:263), unbacked (ledger M-02, wont-fix)
mintedForStable phUSD forwarded to recipient (:264), backed by the deposit
annihilateOneCall.protocolBalanceSheetDelta: assets +stableAmount (at par into the YS); liabilities +(amount + mintedForStable) phUSD. At the intended 1x rate this is 50% collateralised. As the rate degrades the protocol's position IMPROVES (same asset in, less phUSD out) - the shortfall is a pure USER->PROTOCOL transfer, never a protocol-side leak. This is the fact that decides the carve-out question, see ECON-006.

actors.annihilator: supplies real stablecoin + burns AM; is the only party who can lose in this delta
actors.phUSD holders collectively: diluted by the unbacked AM leg (M-02, accepted) and by any above-par issuance (ECON-003)
actors.owner: sets exchangeRate / enabled / paused / maxMintPerDay on the minter; assumed non-malicious (Law 3)

arithmeticCorrections.note: Two upstream claims are arithmetically wrong in the SAME direction (they overstate how easily the stable leg rounds to zero). Corrected here because the econ tier owns the arithmetic of economic claims. Neither correction removes a finding; both narrow one sub-case and leave the main case intact.
arithmeticCorrections.derivation: PhusdStableMinter.calculateMintAmount = (stableAmount * R * 10^(18-dec)) / 1e18 (PhusdStableMinter.sol:254-255). Antimatter guarantees stableAmount * 10^(18-dec) == amount exactly (Antimatter.sol:300-302, INV-10). Substituting: mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18 EXACTLY, for every registered decimals value. The stable's decimals therefore drop out of the economics entirely.

correction1.target: code-scan CODE-003.attackVector: 'for a 6-decimal stable and amount 100e18, mintedForStable reaches 0 for any exchangeRate below 1e16'
correction1.verdict: FALSE. mintedForStable == amount*R/1e18 rounds to zero only when amount*R < 1e18, i.e. R < 1e18/amount. For amount = 100e18 that is R < 0.01, and R is a uint256 - so the ONLY rate producing zero at that size is R == 0 exactly. At R = 1e16 the leg pays 1e18 (1 phUSD), not 0.
correction1.consequence: The ZERO-output end state is reachable only at an exact-zero rate, or on dust annihilations (amount * R < 1e18; the smallest representable amount for a 6-decimal stable is 1e12, which rounds to zero for any R < 1e6, i.e. below 1e-12 of parity). CODE-003's reachable end state stands - test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor executes it - but it should be argued on R == 0 and on the CONTINUOUS partial shortfall, not on a broad near-zero rounding band.

correction2.target: ledger 0ed1c6e3270816c5 (L-03) title: 'A near-zero exchangeRate turns a soft throttle into a hard brick: the stable leg rounds to zero...'
correction2.verdict: Same arithmetic error, inherited from run-01. The rounding band is not broad. The entry needs rewriting anyway (its named guard PhUSDNotReceived no longer exists); the rewrite should adopt the corrected arithmetic rather than carry the band forward.
correction2.flaggedFor: human, at the same time as the CODE-003 re-weigh decision

arithmeticCorrections.whatIsNotNarrowed: The PARTIAL shortfall is continuous and fully reachable for every R in (0, 1e18): shortfall = amount * (1e18 - R) / 1e18 phUSD. That is the economic content of ECON-001 and it needs no rounding edge case at all.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: RECONCILES TO EXISTING LEDGER ENTRY 0ed1c6e3270816c5 (L-03, issueId am1l3, status open, severity low). NO NEW FINGERPRINT IS MINTED. This is the economic half of code-scanner CODE-003 and co-signs its low -> MEDIUM re-weigh recommendation with the value-flow arithmetic CODE-003 did not carry. It must NOT reconcile as `fixed`: the brick L-03 names is gone, but the lines that produced it now settle silently instead of reverting.
findings.description: After story-003 nothing protocol-side requires the stablecoin half to fetch anything. `mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18` (derivation above) is accepted at whatever R the minter holds when the call lands, and the only remaining check is the caller's own combined-total floor at :260, which per CODE-001 is provably inert for every minPhUSDOut in [0, amount]. The stablecoin is already gone by then: it was pulled at :246 and consumed by minter.mint at :251, which deposits it into the yield strategy under the MINTER's ownership (PhusdStableMinter.sol:227-229). PhusdStableMinter exposes no redeem, burn or withdraw of any kind (grep over the whole contract: zero hits), so the deposit is irreversible from the caller's side. The caller cannot get the stablecoin back and cannot get the phUSD it should have fetched.
findings.economicImpact: A pure USER -> PROTOCOL transfer of amount*(1e18-R)/1e18 phUSD-equivalent, borne entirely by the annihilator. The protocol's own position strictly improves (it books the full stablecoin at par and issues less phUSD), so there is no protocol-side leak and nothing here is opportunity cost - see ECON-006.

workedExample.setup: USDC (6 decimals), caller holds 100e18 AM and 100e6 USDC. toStableAmount(USDC, 100e18) = 100e6.
workedExample.intendedOutcome: At R = 1e18 the caller receives 100e18 (AM leg) + 100e18 (stable leg) = 200e18 phUSD. This is the 2x that lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md:99 states is 'antimatter's entire value to a holder'.
workedExample.degradedOutcome: Owner moves R to 6e17 as ordinary depeg management (NatSpec :215-218 sanctions exactly this). mintedForStable = 100e18 * 6e17 / 1e18 = 60e18. totalPhUSD = 160e18.
workedExample.floorIsInert: The caller reasoned in the unit that can actually move and passed minPhUSDOut = 100e18 ('my stable half must fetch at least 100'). 160e18 >= 100e18, so :260 cannot fire. In fact NO value in [0, 100e18] could have fired it, because totalPhUSD >= amount = 100e18 always (profile INV-8).
workedExample.settlement: 100e18 AM burned, 100e6 USDC deposited into the yield strategy permanently, 160e18 phUSD delivered. Caller surrendered $100 of real stablecoin and received $60 of phUSD for it - a 40% loss on the contributed asset, and 80% of the documented 2x.
workedExample.extremeCase: At R = 0 the same call delivers 100e18 phUSD for 100e18 AM + $100 USDC: the stablecoin is surrendered for nothing. Executed verbatim by the project's own test/Annihilation.t.sol:374 test_zeroMinPhUSDOutDisablesFloor, which asserts `usdc.balanceOf(user) == 0` ('the stable half was still taken'). Per arithmeticCorrections.correction1 this exact-zero case needs R == 0 exactly (or a dust amount), not a broad near-zero band.
workedExample.generalForm: loss to caller = amount * (1e18 - R) / 1e18 phUSD, for every R in [0, 1e18). Continuous, no rounding edge case required.

findings.attackScenario: No attacker. annihilate debits msg.sender only (INV-1, INV-2) and credits recipient only (INV-3), so there is no griefing vector and no third party can push a victim into this. The reachable end state is reached by an honest caller whose transaction is in flight across an ordinary owner rate change, or who simply computed the floor in the natural unit.
findings.profitability: n/a as an attack. As a mispricing: the protocol captures amount*(1e18-R)/1e18 per annihilation at no cost and with no signal; a caller has no on-chain way to detect it before the fact, because the pre-burn quote (minter.calculateMintAmount) was deleted and Antimatter no longer reads the minter's pricing surface at all before the burn (profile INV-13).

intentMismatch.documentation: lib/antimatter/CLAUDE.md:99 - 'antimatter's entire value to a holder is that it annihilates into phUSD worth twice its quantity.'
intentMismatch.implementation: src/Antimatter.sol:259-264 - the delivered total is amount + amount*R/1e18, i.e. 1x + R. Twice the quantity holds only at R == 1e18, and at c91bc1a a settlement below that was at least anchored to the minter's own quote and refused outright at zero. At 3a96fb7 any 1x..(1+R)x outcome settles silently.
intentMismatch.discrepancy: The header NatSpec that ledger entry 9d06644ddad24e5a (F-03) already flags for claiming a 2x the code does not guarantee is UNCHANGED at :14-21, and this delta makes that claim strictly weaker: 1x is now a settling outcome rather than a reverting one. F-03 reconciles as unchanged-and-open; its wording is now materially more misleading and is worth a human look.

findings.law3: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun, not as owner malice. See ECON-002 for the lever asymmetry and the safe-config guidance.
findings.severityArgument: Medium, not High: real user asset loss, but it requires an external condition the caller does not control (an owner rate below parity) and a caller floor in the inert range - i.e. C4's 'value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements'. Not Low, because the failure is silent, irreversible, borne by a user who surrendered a real asset, and the NatSpec at :224-225 presents zero as THE opt-out while [1, amount] waives just as completely.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Reinstate a protocol-side floor that does not depend on the caller. Two options, not mutually exclusive: (a) `if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();` immediately after :256 - restores the deleted case at zero cost on the honest path and needs no calculateMintAmount call, so the owner's stated reason for deleting the PRE-BURN quote (redundant, fail-fast only worth gas) does not apply to it; (b) better economically, express the caller's floor on the leg that can actually move - `minStableHalfOut` checked as `mintedForStable < minStableHalfOut` - which has no inert range and matches the unit a caller naturally computes. (b) subsumes CODE-001.

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: GENUINELY NEW as a distinct root cause, but DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS A SEPARATE FINGERPRINT THIS RUN. Its lossy-settlement half is the same reachable end state as ECON-001 / 0ed1c6e3270816c5, and minting a second entry for the same settlement would double-count. What is genuinely new and NOT carried by any entry is the FRONT-RUNNABILITY of the lever (below). Parked visibly here as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance; if a human wants it tracked separately the proposed basis is `src/Antimatter.sol:annihilate:DepegLeverIsNeitherFailSafeNorFrontRunResistant`.
findings.description: PhusdStableMinter offers the owner three superficially interchangeable ways to stand a stablecoin down, and after this delta they no longer fail the same way. `pause()` (enforced PhusdStableMinter.sol:203) and `setStablecoinEnabled(stable,false)` (enforced :206) both REVERT inside minter.mint at Antimatter.sol:251, unwinding the burn and leaving the caller whole - proven by test/Annihilation.t.sol:265 test_pausedMinterRollsEverythingBack. `updateExchangeRate(stable, R)` reverts nowhere: it silently re-prices the stable leg, and at c91bc1a the deleted `expectedForStable == 0 -> PhUSDNotReceived` made the extreme of that lever fail closed too. It no longer does. The lever that reads as the natural depeg response is now the only one of the three that fails LOSSILY, and nothing in either contract distinguishes them.
findings.gameTheoreticContent: Separately from the footgun: `updateExchangeRate` is onlyOwner, unbounded, untimelocked (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138-142) and takes effect only on inclusion, so it is a mempool-visible parameter change. A rate CUT aimed at a depeg can be front-run by exactly the actors it targets - a searcher who sees the pending cut annihilates first at the stale higher rate. A rate RAISE can be back-run. The lever therefore cannot outrun the arbitrage it exists to stop, while the two levers that CAN (pause / disable, both hard reverts) are the ones an owner is least likely to reach for during ordinary rate management. Nothing on the annihilate path consults freshness, a timestamp, or an external oracle (profile: grep for `block.` over src/ returns zero hits).
findings.economicImpact: Two-sided. Downward: in-flight annihilations settle at the new lower rate against inert floors - the ECON-001 loss, borne by users, at a moment the owner believed they were protecting users. Upward/stale: the window between a depeg and the owner's cut is an open arbitrage window - see ECON-003.
findings.attackScenario: 1. A registered stablecoin depegs. 2. Owner submits updateExchangeRate(stable, R_low). 3. A searcher front-runs it, annihilating at the stale R = 1e18 and paying with the depegged asset. 4. The cut lands. 5. Honest callers whose annihilations were already in flight, and who passed a floor in [0, amount], settle at R_low and take the ECON-001 loss. The owner has hit the arbitrageurs with nothing and the honest users with the full shortfall.
findings.profitability: Step 3 nets (1e18 - P_market)/1e18 per unit annihilated for the searcher, bounded by their antimatter balance and the minter's remaining daily cap. Gas-trivial at any meaningful size.
findings.law3: Explicitly NOT a 'malicious owner could' finding - a malicious owner has far better levers and this one is strictly worse for them than pause(). The Law-3 test is whether a competent, non-malicious owner would be SURPRISED that updateExchangeRate(_, 0) settles lossily while pause() reverts safely, and that their rate cut is front-runnable. Both: yes.
safeConfigGuidance: To stand a stablecoin down, use setStablecoinEnabled(stable, false) or pause(). Both revert inside minter.mint and unwind the whole annihilation. NEVER use updateExchangeRate(stable, 0) as a stop - it is not a stop, it is a 100% haircut on every annihilator who does not have a floor strictly above `amount`.

Before any DOWNWARD rate move on a stablecoin that annihilate can reach, disable that stablecoin first, move the rate, then re-enable. That sequences the lossy window behind a reverting one, at the cost of two extra transactions.

Treat a downward rate move as front-runnable: assume every rational holder annihilates at the old rate in the same block. If the depeg is large enough that this matters, reach for pause()/disable, which is atomic in effect, not for the rate.

Independent of this project: PhusdStableMinter.mint has no non-zero-output guard of its own (PhusdStableMinter.sol:242-248 mints whatever calculateMintAmount returns, including 0). Any other integrator of that minter inherits the same lever asymmetry. Out of first-party scope here (nested lib/), recorded so it is not lost.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Antimatter-side: ECON-001's mitigation (a) - a protocol-side `mintedForStable == 0` check - makes the extreme of the rate lever fail closed again, restoring parity with the other two levers at the zero end. It does not address the partial-shortfall or front-running halves, which are minter-side (rate bounds, or a two-step / timelocked rate change).

findings.ledgerCorrespondence: GENUINELY NEW - no existing fingerprint covers cross-stablecoin SELECTION. It must NOT be collapsed into abe4305ac8f0c44f (M-04, wont-fix), which is about the exchangeRate re-pricing only the stable LEG (a within-asset question); this is about WHICH asset the caller pairs with, across assets. Proposed fingerprintBasis `src/Antimatter.sol:annihilate:CallerChoosesCheapestRegisteredStableAtParQuantity` (rootCauseClass CallerChoosesCheapestRegisteredStableAtParQuantity).
findings.notDeltaInduced: PRE-EXISTING at c91bc1a and unchanged by story-003 - the deleted guards never tested freshness or cross-asset price. Filed now because it is genuinely absent from the ledger and Law 1 puts recall above regression-tidiness, NOT because the delta created it. It should be labelled pre-existing wherever it lands.
findings.description: `annihilate` lets the CALLER name which registered stablecoin to pair with (:226), and the pairing is by QUANTITY, not by value: toStableAmount (:283-302) is a pure decimal rescale with no price input whatsoever, so 1 AM always pairs with exactly 1 unit of whichever registered stable the caller picks. The only per-asset price compensation in the whole system is PhusdStableMinter's per-stablecoin `exchangeRate`, which is a manually-maintained, onlyOwner, untimelocked number with no staleness bound and no oracle behind it (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138-142). Nothing on the annihilate path reads a timestamp (profile: zero `block.` hits in src/).
findings.economicImpact: Whenever a registered stablecoin trades below par and its exchangeRate has not yet been cut, every annihilator's dominant strategy is to source that asset. The protocol books a discounted asset at the stale rate and issues phUSD against it, so the discount becomes unbacked phUSD - dilution borne by phUSD holders collectively. This is a genuine value leak, not opportunity cost: the discounted asset is a real asset acquired below the value the protocol credits it at.
findings.attackScenario: 1. Registered stable X depegs to $0.95. 2. Owner has not yet cut R_X from 1e18 (manual, and per ECON-002 front-runnable even once submitted). 3. Holder of N antimatter buys N units of X on the open market for 0.95N. 4. annihilate(X, self, N, 0) delivers N (AM leg) + N (stable leg at the stale rate) = 2N phUSD. 5. Holder contributed N AM plus $0.95N and received $2N of phUSD at peg.
findings.profitability: 0.05N of the 2N is attributable purely to the stale rate - value the protocol credited but never received. Bounded by (i) the attacker's antimatter balance, which is emission-rate-limited, and (ii) the minter's remaining maxMintPerDay, which charges only the stable leg (M-03) so it binds at 2x the configured cap. Gas-trivial at size. The remaining N of unbacked phUSD is the M-02 leg, which the owner has accepted.
affectedParties: the protocol's collateral quality (a discounted asset booked at par)
findings.confidenceCaveat: Medium, not high, for two reasons: the mitigation is entirely minter-side (per-asset rate maintenance), and the owner's M-04 triage reason - 'the exchange rate is there in case of a depeg' - shows the depeg case is a KNOWN and deliberately-handled scenario. What is unaddressed is the LATENCY of that handling and the fact that the caller, not the protocol, picks the asset. If the owner considers manual rate maintenance an accepted operational control, this is QA at most; if not, it is Low bordering Medium.
findings.recommendedMitigation: Minter-side and operational: bound how stale an exchangeRate may be before mint() refuses (a lastRateUpdate timestamp plus a maxRateAge), or drive the rate from an oracle for any stablecoin with meaningful depeg history. Antimatter-side there is nothing to fix - it correctly defers pricing to the minter (:214-218) - so this belongs on the operational-hazard channel rather than as a code change to src/Antimatter.sol.

findings.question: Scan item 2 - with overpayment now forwarded, does the removal of the upside bound RE-ARM or WIDEN M-02 (64807f2b1456d622) or M-04 (abe4305ac8f0c44f)?
findings.verdict: NO to both, and the code-scanner's MR-03-04 overstates this. The removal widens exactly ONE dimension - unattributed mid-call phUSD - which is already carried by ad4b779566291190 (L-01) via code-scan CODE-002. No new fingerprint is minted, and neither wont-fix entry is re-filed or re-weighed.

reasoning.whyM04IsNotReArmed: The deleted check was `mintedForStable != expectedForStable`, where `expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount)` - computed in the SAME transaction, from the SAME `config.exchangeRate` storage slot that minter.mint then uses (PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 calls the identical function). The two values were therefore EQUAL by construction for any rate, above parity or below; the owner cannot change the rate mid-transaction (updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner and re-entry into it is impossible from this path). The old check consequently NEVER bounded a rate above parity. M-04's 'unbounded ceiling' was already fully live at c91bc1a and is unchanged at 3a96fb7.
reasoning.testEvidenceMisread: test/Annihilation.t.sol:335 test_overPhUSDMintNowSucceeds is cited by MR-03-04 as proof the ceiling bound was lost. It is not: it sets R = 15e17 BEFORE the call, so at c91bc1a expectedForStable would also have been 150e18, the equality would have held, and the old code would have succeeded identically. The test's own comment ('Overpayment is no longer refused') describes an effect the deleted check did not have. Correcting this matters because reading it the other way would mint a duplicate fingerprint against a wont-fix.
reasoning.whatWasActuallyLost: The equality check bounded the phUSD balance delta against a QUOTE, so its only real reach was a delta whose source was NOT the minter's mint for this deposit - i.e. phUSD injected onto Antimatter inside the window [:244, :256] by the registered stable's transfer hook or anything it calls. A one-sided floor is structurally incapable of catching an over-credit (an injection RAISES totalPhUSD and therefore passes :260 by construction).
reasoning.whyM02IsNotWidened: M-02 is the AM leg - `_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount)` at :263, driven verbatim by `amount` with no rate, no branch and no quote between (profile minPhUSDOutSemantics.unconditional1to1Half). The delta touches neither the quantity nor the condition of that mint. M-02 is byte-for-byte unchanged.

findings.isThereAMintAgainstValueNeverDeposited: YES, but not newly. Two such paths exist and both predate the delta: (i) the AM leg, which is M-02 and is owner-accepted; (ii) an above-par rate, which is M-04's ceiling and equally reachable through PhusdStableMinter.mint directly with no antimatter involved at all - so annihilate is not the enabling surface. Crucially there is NO round-trip: PhusdStableMinter has no redeem, burn or withdraw entry point (grep over the whole contract: zero hits), so over-issued phUSD cannot be cycled back through the protocol for the underlying. Any realisation is secondary-market, which caps the extractable amount at market depth rather than at protocol reserves. That is why this is dilution, not a drain, and why it does not escalate.

M-02.triageReason: "The no-collateral mint is just one side of the bookkeeping. In reality, antimatter was generated from prior stablecoin staked in the vaults. So it is value in the protocol that has already been generated. It's now just being rewarded."
M-02.basisForRevisiting: NONE. Not revisited, not re-weighed, not re-filed. Examined only to answer whether this delta widened it; it did not.

M-04.triageReason: "The stable leg is handled by phUSD-minter stable security. The exchange rate is there in case of a depeg. But the 1:1 with antimatter is unrelated. The antimatter was earned elsewhere. It already has its value. phUSD is just realizing that."
M-04.basisForRevisiting: NONE for the ceiling. Recorded only to correct MR-03-04's claim that this delta re-armed it. Note separately that ECON-001 sits at the OTHER end of the same lever - the owner's triage says the rate exists 'in case of a depeg', and ECON-001 shows that using it for exactly that purpose is now lossy to users. That is a NEW consequence of a NEW commit, not a re-litigation of M-04, and it is filed on 0ed1c6e3270816c5.

findings.question: Scan item 3 - does the delta change the cap arithmetic or the DoS surface, and is it true that a binding cap now produces a smaller mintedForStable rather than a revert?
findings.hypothesisTested: 'A cap that binds now produces a smaller mintedForStable rather than a revert.'
findings.verdict: THE HYPOTHESIS IS FALSE. Verified against source: PhusdStableMinter.sol:221 is `require(config.mintedToday + phUSDAmount <= config.maxMintPerDay, "Daily mint limit exceeded")`. It is a REVERT, not a clamp - there is no partial-fill path anywhere in mint(), and phUSDAmount is computed in full at :212 before the cap is consulted. A binding cap therefore reverts inside minter.mint at Antimatter.sol:251, which unwinds the burn, the pull and the approval, leaving the caller whole. The delta does not touch this: the cap is charged and enforced entirely inside the minter, on a line the story did not go near.
findings.capArithmeticUnchanged: The cap is still charged `phUSDAmount` = the STABLE leg only (PhusdStableMinter.sol:212, :222), while annihilate additionally mints `amount` at Antimatter.sol:263 outside the minter entirely. A cap of X still permits 2X at parity. That is M-03 (df5c16e2238a3c1c) and M-05 (6a6a6bcba7b0dff1) verbatim, both wont-fix, both unchanged by this delta. Run-02's Tier-3 invariant failures (invariant_9: charged 332000000000000, issued 664000000000000) remain the authoritative quantification.
findings.dosSurfaceUnchanged: Cap exhaustion is still an availability failure that reverts safely (revertConditions list, profile: "Daily mint limit exceeded" at :251). No new DoS surface, and none removed.

oneGenuineDeltaInducedConsequence.statement: The cap's BINDING POWER now degrades continuously with the exchange rate, and at R == 0 it vanishes entirely while unbacked issuance continues at full rate.
oneGenuineDeltaInducedConsequence.arithmetic: The cap charge is mintedForStable = amount * R / 1e18, so the number of antimatter units that fit under a cap of X in one window is X * 1e18 / R, while each of them mints `amount` uncapped phUSD at :263. Total window issuance is therefore X * (1 + 1e18/R), which diverges as R falls: at R = 1e18 the cap admits 2X; at R = 1e17 it admits 11X; at R = 0 the charge is 0 and the cap is entirely non-binding while the AM leg still issues without limit.
oneGenuineDeltaInducedConsequence.whyThisIsDeltaInduced: At c91bc1a the R == 0 corner was UNREACHABLE - `expectedForStable == 0 -> PhUSDNotReceived` reverted pre-burn, so the cap could never be driven to a zero charge through annihilate. At 3a96fb7 that corner settles. The intermediate degradation (R below parity shrinking the charge) is M-04's 'silent re-scaling of what maxMintPerDay permits' and is NOT new; only the endpoint is.
oneGenuineDeltaInducedConsequence.economicWeight: LOW in practice, and deliberately not filed as its own finding. The states in which the cap is neutralised are exactly the states in which annihilating is against the caller's own interest (ECON-001), so the volume that would flow through the neutralised cap is limited to callers who do not realise their floor is inert. It is a control degradation, not an independent extraction path.
oneGenuineDeltaInducedConsequence.ledgerCorrespondence: CORROBORATION ON df5c16e2238a3c1c (M-03). NO NEW FINGERPRINT. Recorded so the endpoint is visible in this run's record.

M-03.triageReason: "If the quantity of phUSD produced from this is excessive, we will have to reduce it at its source (phUSDminter). But antimatter is generated as an emission, a yield. So it's very likely to just not be on the same order of magnitude as the principals we're worrying about."
M-03.basisForRevisiting: NOT revisited and NOT re-weighed. The owner's disposal rests on annihilation volume being small relative to principals, which the endpoint above does not contradict - it changes the cap's leverage, not the emission rate that bounds it. Recorded as corroboration only, exactly as run-02 recorded its invariant failures against this entry.

M-05.triageReason: "Again this same budget thing is misleading. Antimatter earned its legs elsewhere."
M-05.basisForRevisiting: NONE. Unchanged by this delta. The shared-budget asymmetry it names is a property of where the cap is charged, which the story did not touch.

findings.question: Scan item 5 - does the externally-derived-yield / opportunity-cost carve-out cover any candidate in this run?
findings.verdict: NO CANDIDATE IN THIS RUN IS COVERED. The carve-out is applied and comes back negative on every finding; nothing was suppressed under it.

perFinding.reason: The loss is borne by a USER who surrendered a real stablecoin from their own balance at Antimatter.sol:246 and cannot recover it (PhusdStableMinter has no redeem path). This is not a pot funded by yield on protocol-owned capital; it is a transfer of third-party principal. The carve-out explicitly does not reach it, and the direction is the opposite of the carve-out's shape anyway: the PROTOCOL gains, so there is no protocol-side pot to misallocate.
Same underlying settlement as ECON-001 plus a searcher-extraction path; neither involves protocol-owned yield.

The dilution is against phUSD holders' claim on real deposited collateral, arising from a discounted asset booked at par. That is a reduction in backing, not a distribution of externally-derived yield.

perFinding.covered: ARGUABLY - and this is precisely the owner's own triage reasoning ('antimatter was generated from prior stablecoin staked in the vaults... value in the protocol that has already been generated'). Consistent with the carve-out. Not re-filed, not re-weighed, mentioned only for completeness.

findings.inverseCheckPerformed: Also checked the opposite error - filing a protocol-side value leak that does not exist. rows.verdict: NO ROUNDING FINDING - one direction verified favourable, one N/A
rows.basis: There is exactly one division on the value path: PhusdStableMinter.calculateMintAmount's `/ 1e18` (:255), a solidity integer division that rounds DOWN on what the USER RECEIVES. That is the safe direction per the table (round down on user receipts). Antimatter's own toStableAmount (:300-302) does not round at all - it enforces an exact integer round-trip and reverts AmountNotRepresentable otherwise (INV-10), so no dust accrues on the pairing. There is NO round-trip in this protocol: no redeem, burn or withdraw exists on PhusdStableMinter (grep, zero hits), so the composed-round-trip row of the table has no instance to evaluate and no first-depositor / inflation surface exists. No symmetric or banker's rounding anywhere. No fee is taken on either leg.
No accumulator on the path. mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18 exactly, per-call, with no carried remainder and no per-share index.
Neither contract charges a fee on the annihilate path.

The only price input in the system is PhusdStableMinter.exchangeRate, a manually-maintained onlyOwner scalar with no staleness bound and no external oracle. Antimatter reads no price at all after this delta (INV-13).
No TWAP, no AMM read, no block.timestamp anywhere in src/ (profile weakRandomness, verified zero `block.` hits).

Nothing on the path prices off a balance or a reserve. The pairing is a fixed-quantity decimal rescale and the phUSD output is a fixed linear function of `amount` and a stored scalar. A flash loan of the stablecoin buys nothing: annihilate additionally requires burning an equal quantity of antimatter, which is emission-limited and cannot be flash-borrowed from any in-scope contract.

rows.verdict: NOTED - the asymmetry IS M-04, unchanged
rows.basis: Antimatter prices the AM leg at a hardcoded 1:1 while the minter prices the stable leg at R. Two different prices for the same phUSD unit in one transaction. That is abe4305ac8f0c44f, wont-fix, and this delta does not change it (ECON-004).

rows.verdict: FILED - ECON-002 (front-running a rate cut), ECON-003 (depeg window)

rows.basis: annihilate debits msg.sender only (INV-1, INV-2) and credits recipient only (INV-3). No third party can be pushed into any of the states above. The one third-party-influenced quantity, mintedForStable, can only be raised by an outsider (CODE-002 / ad4b779566291190), never lowered.
No borrowing, no collateral ratio, no liquidation anywhere in either contract.

rows.verdict: N/A under Law 3 for malice; the non-obvious slice is FILED as ECON-002
rows.basis: All parameters are plain onlyOwner setters with no token governance.

A profitable cycle needs a way back. PhusdStableMinter is mint-only: no redeem, burn or withdraw entry point exists (grep over the whole contract, zero hits), and antimatter itself has no mint path open to an annihilator (Antimatter.mint is onlyApprovedMinters, :192). The graph is acyclic, so no loop can be pumped. This is the single most load-bearing structural fact keeping ECON-003 and M-02/M-04 at dilution rather than drain.
Per-stablecoin config is isolated in the minter's mapping; each has its own rate, cap and window. One stablecoin's cap exhaustion does not touch another's.

The annihilator's optimal timing (annihilate when R is highest) is directly opposed to the owner's depeg response (cut R), and the annihilator wins the race because the cut is mempool-visible - ECON-002. Every other actor's incentives are aligned or inert.

manualReview.title: The economics no longer depend on the stable's decimals at all - one fewer variable than the ledger's framing assumes
manualReview.why: Because Antimatter enforces stableAmount * 10^(18-dec) == amount exactly, the decimalAdjustment in calculateMintAmount cancels perfectly and mintedForStable == amount * R / 1e18 for EVERY registered decimals value. Several ledger entries and CODE-003 reason about 6-decimal vs 18-decimal cases as if they differed economically; they do not. Recorded so future runs stop re-deriving per-decimals cases, and because it is what makes the arithmeticCorrections above provable rather than empirical.

manualReview.title: PhusdStableMinter.mint's missing non-zero-output guard is the shared root cause and is outside first-party scope
